## A diffusion model, from nodes

The thing a KSampler runs. Stripped of the engineering it is three sentences:

1. **Mix** a picture with noise, by a random amount `t` between nothing and everything.
2. **Train** an ordinary network to look at the mess and say *which part was the noise*.
3. **Sample** by starting from pure noise, asking the network what the noise is, taking a
little of it away, and going round again.

Step 2 is a plain supervised problem, which is why the same **Train** node that fits a
classifier also fits this. All of the interesting part is step 3, and step 3 is a for loop.

### 1 — Make the data

**Dataset As Diffusion** takes the 480 bundled shape pictures and, for each one, rolls a
random noise level and mixes it in. The **noise it added** becomes the answer.

Nothing here is labelled. The supervision is manufactured, so any folder of pictures is
already a complete training set.

`copies` decides how many noise levels each picture is seen at — the network has to be
good at every point of the journey, not only the middle.

### Why the input has **5** channels

The network cannot do its job without knowing *how noisy* its input is: the same grey
smudge means one thing at `t=0.1` and another at `t=0.9`.

So the timestep travels with the picture — 3 colour channels plus 2 channels holding a
sine/cosine encoding of `t`. Real implementations inject it inside every block; here it
arrives on the wire where you can see it.

Try setting `time_channels` to **0**. The model can no longer tell how far along it is,
and it produces mud.

### 2 — The network is just a U-Net

The same shape as example 10, and it has no idea it is doing anything generative. Down
through the encoder, across the bottom, back up the decoder, with the two **Concat** nodes
carrying full-resolution detail past the middle.

The last **Conv 2D** brings it back to 3 channels: one guess at the noise, per pixel.

Note the asymmetry — 5 channels in, 3 channels out. It is fed the timestep and it is not
asked to predict one.

### 3 — Ordinary training

No special loss, no special optimiser. `mse` between the noise the network guessed and
the noise that was actually added.

Watch the loss curve: it drops fast and then crawls. The crawl is where the picture
quality lives, so this one is worth leaving to run.

**About eight minutes on a CPU**, and early stopping ends it when it stops improving. In a
hurry? Set `epochs` to 60 — you get the idea in ninety seconds, just blurrier.

### 4 — Sample from it

**Sample (Diffusion)** runs the loop backwards from pure noise. The `dataset` input is
not for data — it carries the noise schedule the model trained with, so the two cannot
drift apart.

`steps` is a speed dial: the sampler is deterministic, so 60 steps should look like 20.
If it does not, something is wrong.

The second output is **one frame per step** — feed it to a video node and watch the
picture appear out of the noise.

Things to try: `guidance` above 0 sharpens an undertrained model. `predict: image`
asks the network to guess the clean picture instead of the noise — easier to imagine, and
it still samples.
